a S
Prefix sums (前缀和): S[i] = a[1] + … + a[i], with S[0] = 0. Building S takes one pass; then the sum of any range a[l..r] is S[r] − S[l − 1] in O(1), instead of O(r − l) by adding.
Use 1-based indexing so that S[0] = 0 exists and l = 1 needs no special case.
Sums can exceed int: store S as long long .
With m queries on n numbers, adding each range costs O(nm); prefix sums cost O(n + m). This is the first tool to try whenever a problem asks for many range sums (P8218).
S[i][j] = sum of the rectangle from (1, 1) to (i, j). Build and query by inclusion–exclusion:
The corner S[i−1][j−1] is counted twice when adding the strip above and the strip to the left, so subtract it once. In a query, the corner is subtracted twice, so add it back.

Maximum-sum rectangle: fix the top and bottom rows (O(n²) pairs); the column sums between them form a 1D array, and the best range of columns is the maximum subarray of 第1章 . Column prefix sums give each value in O(1): O(n³) in total (P1719).
Binary search on a parameter, with prefix sums so that each check is O(n), solves the quality inspector (P1314); splitting brownies into an even grid checks each guess with 2D prefix sums (P3017).
Range updates as two point changes; 2D corners.
a d

Difference array (差分): d[i] = a[i] − a[i − 1]. Adding v to a whole range a[l..r] changes only two entries: d[l] += v, d[r + 1] −= v. After all updates, a prefix sum over d rebuilds a. Range updates become O(1) each.
Prefix sums and differences undo each other: prefix sums answer many range queries, differences apply many range updates. Use differences when all updates come before all queries.

Changing a range by ±1 changes one difference up and one down (or one at the ends). To make all values equal, every d[2..n] must become 0: pair a positive with a negative while both exist, then fix the rest alone, so the answer is max(pos, neg) operations (P4552). Ticket counting per rail segment (P3406) and checking orders for classrooms with binary search (P1083) are difference arrays too.

Adding 1 to a rectangle touches four corners of the 2D difference array. A 2D prefix sum afterwards turns the corners back into the full counts: O(1) per carpet and O(n²) once at the end, instead of O(n²) per carpet (P3397).
Flipping k cows at a time with as few flips as possible keeps a running difference of "flips still active" while scanning (P2882).
sort, unique, lower_bound: values to ranks.
value → its rank among the distinct values

Discretisation (离散化): when only the order of values matters, not their size, replace each value by its rank among the distinct values. Coordinates up to 109 become 0 … n − 1, small enough to index an array.
Recipe: copy the values, sort , unique + erase , then rank(x) = lower_bound(v.begin(), v.end(), x) - v.begin() . O(n log n).

The sorted endpoints cut the line into at most 2n pieces; inside one piece nothing changes. A difference array over the piece numbers counts how many intervals cover each piece, and covered pieces add their real length xs[i + 1] − xs[i] (P1496).

In 2D, the sorted x and y coordinates cut the plane into at most 2n × 2n cells; a 2D difference marks which cells are covered and each covered cell adds its real area (P1884). Program analysis with huge variable numbers discretises before union-find (P1955); skylines (P1904), cow line-ups (P3029) and parity games (P5937) compress coordinates the same way.
After discretising, distance is lost: ranks 3 and 4 may be far apart in reality. Always add back the real length (xs[i + 1] − xs[i] ) when measuring, and keep both ends of every interval in the list.
